question: What temperature will be required for the preparation of Plaster of Paris from gypsum?
solution:
The correct answer is __**100°C.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plaster of Paris** is a **white powder** obtained by **heating gypsum **at a temperature of **100-150oC.**
 
• When gypsum is heated to this temperature, it loses about** three-quarters **of its** water of crystallization** and forms a fine powder known as Plaster of Paris.
 
• This powder can be mixed with water to form a **paste**, which can be used to** cast molds, sculptures**, and **other decorative objects.**
 
• The** setting time **of Plaster of Paris is** relatively short**, making it an ideal material for** casting small objects**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **quantity of water molecules** that **combines chemically** in a specific** molecular proportion** with the relevant salt in a crystalline state is known as the **water of crystallization.** 
 
• The crystals' geometric** form and color** are the result of this water.
 
• It is a crystal structure made of **water bound together** chemically.
